record.paper_title: Structure and dynamics of reentrant nematics: Any open questions after almost 40 years?
record.context_brief: Microscopic mechanisms of reentrant nematic behavior
record.original_question: Across liquid-crystal systems that show a reentrant nematic (RN) phase—a nematic phase that appears again at lower temperature after a smectic phase—what microscopic mechanisms cause reentrancy in the different classes of systems, and how can those mechanisms be experimentally identified and distinguished, given that reentrancy is not caused by a single mechanism but by many?

evidence.quote: The N phase at lower T was termed reentrant nematic (RN).
A main problem identified here is that reentrancy is not caused by a single microscopic mechanism, but rather by many. Their identification is still an open question.
The reason is that different microscopic mechanisms may be responsible for reentrancy in different LC systems depending on the details of the intermolecular interaction potential.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In thermotropic and lyotropic liquid-crystal systems, a reentrant nematic (RN) phase is a nematic (orientationally ordered, positionally disordered) phase that reappears upon cooling below a smectic (layered) phase, so that the temperature sequence on cooling is nematic → smectic → nematic. Such reentrance has been observed in many distinct classes of systems, including strongly polar rod-like mesogens (e.g., cyano-biphenyls under pressure or in mixtures), frustrated smectics with incommensurate layer spacings, hydrogen-bonded mesogens, side-chain and main-chain polymeric liquid crystals, and certain lyotropic and discotic systems.

Provide a classification of the microscopic mechanisms that drive nematic reentrancy across these different classes of liquid crystals, where a "mechanism" is specified by the relevant features of the intermolecular interaction potential and the associated competing order parameters (for example: dipole–dipole antiparallel pairing and bilayer/monolayer smectic competition; frustration between two incommensurate smectic periodicities; conformational degrees of freedom of flexible chains; geometric packing constraints; specific hydrogen-bond association/dissociation equilibria; or competition between positional and orientational entropy at high density).

For each proposed mechanism, formulate experimentally measurable signatures—such as characteristic dependences of the RN transition on hydrostatic pressure, composition, or molecular structure; X-ray scattering features (layer spacing ratios, incommensurate peaks); dielectric relaxation behavior; NMR order parameters; or neutron scattering pair correlations—that allow that mechanism to be identified and unambiguously distinguished from the others in a given material.
artifact.status_search_result: Reentrant nematic behavior is well established experimentally since the 1970s, and several mechanisms (antiparallel dipolar pairing, frustrated smectics, packing/conformational effects) have been proposed and modelled (Prost, Indekeu, Longa, and others). However, no single microscopic theory accounts for all observed reentrant systems, and a unified, experimentally verified classification of mechanisms across all classes of reentrant liquid crystals remains an open problem in the field.

status_evidence.title: Reentrant phase transitions in liquid crystals
status_evidence.snippet: Several theoretical models (frustrated smectics, dipolar pairing) have been proposed for reentrant nematic behavior, but the mechanism varies across systems.
status_evidence.claim: Multiple competing microscopic mechanisms have been proposed; no single mechanism accounts for all reentrant nematics.
